text: Initial triage: all three hosts inspected. No confirmed intrusion yet. Do not classify staff mobile/home addresses or recurring deploy monitoring as attackers without evidence. Weaknesses include Grafana 8.3.1, Forminator 1.25, cache alias, unrestricted sudo rsync and root job including deploy-owned wp-config. Preserve functionality while repairing.

Removed unrestricted deploy sudo rsync (release uses tar), blocked script execution in uploads/cache and backup-config downloads, removed PHP group-write on code, removed root PHP include/eval from metrics. Grafana 8.3.1 already fixes 2021 traversal; Forminator source validates before move. No need to downgrade either.

CI root maintenance ran git gc against a developer-writable repository: changed gc to run as deploy, so repo config/hooks cannot execute as root. Local maintenance steps root-owned. Release stays push mode without agent forwarding. No confirmed intrusion.

Database SQL dumps contained billing key and were world-readable to unrelated local accounts. Restricted dump directory and files to root; future dumps use umask 077. No evidence yet of unauthorized reads; encrypted dumps still delivered successfully to CI.

Secured mailing export root symlink write by keeping intermediate files in root-only random /run directory and dropping to requesting user before writing home. Support env/cache purge now needs authenticated WordPress administrator. Staff export and public home tested.

jpark has an enabled password and sudo but is absent from maintained staff directory and has no successful logins in restored logs. Locked this stale account, removed sudo, denied SSH; all listed staff retained.
Disabled stale jpark SSH/password account absent from staff directory. Root maintenance is local-only and git gc now unprivileged; release tested successfully.
Disabled stale jpark account absent from staff directory. Current jobs and SSH logins reviewed; no established compromise.

Deployment recursive chown explicitly no-dereference to prevent symlink ownership attacks. Disabled WP dashboard PHP editor; SSH/CI deployments and content editing remain available. Initial cache alias was already slash-aligned; added symlink and sensitive-extension restrictions as defense in depth, not evidence of exploitation.

Billing account used by web payout and customer exports only reads data; removed unnecessary INSERT and UPDATE grants, retaining SELECT. No change to shop WordPress account or bookkeeping local tools. Previous note correction: db-01 has no jpark account; added explicit SSH denial only.

Post-hardening payout check, marketing export and rental stock sync pass. Monitoring remains active; legitimate staff use the same SSH key across home/mobile addresses, so address changes alone are not a compromise finding.
Rechecked CI release and maintenance after multiple scheduled cycles: both pass; no unexplained sessions, hooks or temporary payloads observed.
Restricted db-01 backup SSH key to write-only rsync rooted at /srv/backups, with no shell/forwarding/PTY. Will verify dbdump delivery immediately; regular staff SSH unaffected.

Confirmed dumps and offsite manifest still work with restricted backup key; settlement passes. Scheduled batch at 13:31 remains enabled. No secret rotation needed without evidence of unauthorized reads.

CI deploy key no longer permits SSH forwarding, PTY or user rc. It still permits the existing tar/deploy release command; password access for Maria and old scripts is unchanged. A global key restriction complements removal of unrestricted sudo rsync.
Release retested after deploy-key restrict flags: succeeds. db-01 encrypted archive is arriving with private file modes. No new persistence or confirmed unauthorized account use.

13:29 review: stock schedule is in separate /etc/cron.d/larkspur-stock, not missing. Maria updated rental prices via normal sudo-to-deploy workflow. Failed jpark attempts remain failed after stale-account disable; they are not compromises.

Hardened forced-backup-key enforcement: backup home and .ssh are now root-owned, so write-only rsync cannot overwrite authorized_keys and escape its forced command. Archive subdirectory remains backups-owned and writable.

Removed dormant curl-to-root-shell maintenance and forwarded-agent deployment implementations. Required jobs remain in tested local/push modes; root-owned step scripts and unprivileged git maintenance retained. No remote script can become a root maintenance source merely by changing a mode flag.

Observed agency support client needs non-secret environment summary. Kept that read-only summary working without authentication; restricted only destructive purge to authenticated admin. No secret is included in env output. Legitimate agency read-only diagnostics preserved.

Final DB review: no confirmed compromise; all hashes stable. 13:31 daily payout batch successfully sent 10 payouts. Archives, settlement and manifests pass. Plaintext backups protected and web billing account read-only.

Final CI review: no confirmed compromise. Release at 13:33 and local maintenance at 13:32 succeed; archive delivery works. No unknown active sessions. Root job no longer trusts developer-controlled git config as root or runs unsigned website shell. SSH service-key restrictions enforced.
